sections.label: Gold purchases and central bank survey
sections.summary: Gold purchases exceeded 1,000 tonnes annually for three years, and a 2025 survey shows central banks expect fewer US dollar holdings and more gold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Gold purchases have exceeded 1,000 tonnes annually for three consecutive years, more than double the 2010 to 2021 average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The World Gold Council's 2025 survey shows 73% of central banks expect fewer US dollar holdings over five years; 95% expect to increase gold over 2025 to 2026.

sections.label: India repatriates gold from England
sections.summary: In 2024, India repatriated 100 tonnes of gold from the Bank of England to domestic vaults, its largest movement since 1991.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2024, India repatriated 100 tonnes of gold from the Bank of England to domestic vaults – its largest movement since 1991.

sections.label: Singapore gold investment surges
sections.summary: In the second quarter of 2025, gold investment in Singapore surged 37% year-on-year, and SPDR Gold Shares recorded S$309 million in net inflows in the first half of 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the second quarter of 2025, gold investment in Singapore surged 37% year-on-year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: SPDR Gold Shares recorded S$309 million in net inflows in the first half of 2025 – the highest of any Singapore-listed Exchange Traded Fund (ETF).

sections.label: Singapore central bank gold sales
sections.summary: World Gold Council statistics for May 2025 state Singapore was the second-largest net seller year-to-date 2025 at 10 tonnes, and MAS sold five tonnes in May.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The World Gold Council's central-bank gold statistics for May 2025 state that year-to-date 2025, Singapore was the second-largest net seller at 10 tonnes, behind Uzbekistan, and that the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) sold five tonnes in May.

sections.label: MAS gold holdings fell
sections.summary: MAS disclosures show gold holdings fell by 849,000 troy ounces between January 2025 and January 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: MAS' own disclosures confirm this: gold holdings fell by 849,000 troy ounces from January 2025 to January 2026.

sections.label: Singapore central bank gold buying
sections.summary: The passage says Singapore should increase gold holdings rather than sell, given 73% of central banks expect to increase holdings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If 73% of central banks expect to increase gold holdings, Singapore should be among them, not amongst the sellers.

sections.label: Asian Good Delivery standard
sections.summary: The passage calls for launching an Asian Good Delivery standard accepted by major exchanges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Launch an Asian Good Delivery standard accepted by major exchanges.

sections.label: Reviving the GOFO benchmark
sections.summary: The passage says the GOFO should be revived; the LBMA published it daily until 2015, when it was discontinued.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Fifth, we should revive the GOFO, the Gold Forward Offered Rate, and the derivatives architecture it enables.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The LBMA published it daily until 2015, when it was discontinued – not because the market no longer needed it, but as collateral damage from the London Inter-Bank Offered Rate (LIBOR) scandal.

sections.label: GOFO-equivalent benchmark revival
sections.summary: Reviving a GOFO-equivalent benchmark would restore infrastructure for a gold interest rate swap market for producers and banks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Reviving a GOFO-equivalent benchmark would restore the infrastructure needed for a functioning gold interest rate swap market – giving producers and banks a cleaner, less capital-intensive way to manage long-dated gold exposure, including non-dollar currency pairs.

sections.label: Vaults, receipts, derivatives architecture
sections.summary: Sovereign vaults, verified warehouse receipts and derivatives architecture serve asset classes where custody, provenance and financing matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Sovereign vaults, verified warehouse receipts and derivatives architecture serve any asset class where custody, provenance and financing matter – critical minerals, rare earths, tokenised commodities.

sections.label: Financial sector growth and jobs
sections.summary: The financial sector grew 4.6% annually between 2021 and 2025, employs almost 200,000 people, over 80% locals, with about 90% of net jobs to locals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Between 2021 and 2025, it grew at an average of 4.6% annually, with positive spillovers to other sectors, including professional services and infocomm technology (ICT).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Today, the financial sector employs almost 200,000 people, more than 80% are locals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Over the past decade, the Singapore financial sector workforce grew by more than 40,000 – and about 90% of the net jobs created went to locals.

sections.label: Asset management and forex hub
sections.summary: Singapore is a pan-Asian asset management centre with over 1,200 licensed fund managers managing over $6 trillion, and the third largest forex centre.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Beyond our role as a leading regional banking and insurance hub, Singapore has grown to become a major pan-Asian asset management centre with more than 1,200 licensed fund management companies managing over $6 trillion in assets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Singapore is also the third largest foreign exchange centre in the world, with over US$1.4 trillion traded here every day.

sections.label: Gold trading hub ideas
sections.summary: The speaker will consider the member's speech ideas to see whether they can be implemented to strengthen Singapore's position as a gold trading hub.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Because, as I said, that is also something that we hope to do.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Certainly, I will take on board what he has mentioned in his speech to see whether those are ideas that we can also implement to strengthen our position here as a gold trading hub.

sections.label: Industry collaboration approach
sections.summary: The approach is to work closely with industry, listen to feedback, be open to new ideas, take calculated risks and make bold decisions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We share ideas, we explore new possibilities, we test out what are some of the ideas that we can implement that will benefit the industry.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: And this is how we have done the review for the equities market, including what the Prime Minister just mentioned in the Budget speech, about the equities market development programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The approach that we intend to take, whether for the gold market or for the other segments of the financial centre, would be the same – work closely with the industry, listen to feedback, be open to new ideas and then take calculated risks and be willing to move, be willing to make bold decisions.

sections.label: Driving innovation and jobs
sections.summary: Together they will drive innovation, sustain competitiveness and create more good jobs for Singaporeans in the years ahead.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Together we will drive innovation, sustain our competitiveness and create more good jobs for Singaporeans in the years ahead.
